subject.title: fix(codex): continue after source-reply delivery instead of terminating turn

question: Does current `main` intentionally supersede both source-reply fix branches, or should this PR or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107388 remain the canonical landing candidate?
rationale: The submitted patch is internally sound, but current-main drift and two overlapping implementations make branch selection and exactly-once delivery ownership a maintainer choice after live proof.

options.title: Treat current main as canonical
options.body: Confirm the current-main refactor intentionally provides explicit-only termination and adequate regression coverage, then close both overlapping branches as redundant.

options.title: Keep this PR canonical
options.body: Rebase this branch, retain its broader regression coverage, add live Discord/Codex exactly-once proof, and close the overlapping candidate.

options.title: Use the competing PR
options.body: Select https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107388 if its schema-description change is desired, require equivalent live proof, and close this branch.

recommendation.title: Treat current main as canonical
recommendation.body: Confirm the current-main refactor intentionally provides explicit-only termination and adequate regression coverage, then close both overlapping branches as redundant.
